Why retries turn instability into a self-inflicted attack
Bulkhead isolation changes the system model
Circuit breakers stop panic before it spreads
Build for controlled degradation, not perfect uptime

takeaways: In distributed .NET systems, a slow dependency often does more damage than a crashed one because waiting work quietly consumes threads, sockets and queue capacity.
Retries should only be used for brief, random faults; against an overloaded dependency they multiply pressure, so bulkheads and scoped circuit breakers are needed to contain the blast radius.
Resilience is a business policy: define service quality tiers, degraded modes and per-dependency rules for timeout, retry, breaker, fallback and isolation, then test them deliberately.
hook: Your microservices look healthy, yet capacity is silently collapsing behind one slow dependency. This episode is for .NET architects and engineering leaders who want to understand cascading latency failures. Learn how bulkheads, circuit breakers and controlled degradation keep one slow call from taking down the whole platform.
